sets.title: Alphanumeric series
sets.stimulus:
Study the following arrangement carefully and answer the questions given below.

**P 4 @ R E 7 # 2 M 9 % U 1 T £ B 6 & 3 A W ★ H 8**

questions.prompt: How many such numbers are there in the above arrangement, each of which is immediately preceded by a letter and immediately followed by a symbol?

steps: Check each number: it needs a letter just before it and a symbol just after it.
Such numbers: 4 → **More than three**.
solution.shortcut: Scan only the numbers and glance at the element on each side — no need to read every element.
solution.trap: U **1** T does not count — it is followed by T, not a symbol.

questions.prompt: How many such symbols are there in the above arrangement, each of which is immediately preceded by a number and immediately followed by a letter?

steps: Check each symbol: it needs a number just before it and a letter just after it.
Such symbols: 2 → **Two**.
solution.shortcut: Scan only the symbols and glance at the element on each side — no need to read every element.
solution.trap: 7 **#** 2 does not count — it is followed by 2, not a letter.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the 9th element from the right end in the above arrangement?

steps: 9th from the right end = 24 − 9 + 1 = 16th from the left end (**B**).
16th from the left end = **B**.
solution.shortcut: From the right end, position = n − m + 1 = 24 − 9 + 1 = 16.
solution.trap: Counting from the left end gives **M**.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the 6th element to the right of the 8th element from the left end in the above arrangement?

steps: 8th from the left end = **2**.
6th to the right of it = 8 + 6 = 14th from the left end.
14th from the left end = **T**.
solution.shortcut: Convert to one count from the left: 8th + 6 = 14th.
solution.trap: Moving 6 to the left instead gives **4**.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the 5th element to the left of **★** in the above arrangement?

steps: **★** is 22nd from the left end.
5th to the left → 17th from the left end (**6**).
solution.shortcut: Net movement = −5 = −5 → 5 to the left of ★.
solution.trap: Do not count ★ itself as the first step — starting the count on ★ lands on **&**, one place short.

sets.title: Alphanumeric series
sets.stimulus:
Study the following arrangement carefully and answer the questions given below.

**5 D © 8 I N 3 ↑ P 2 = Q 6 # O L 9 \$ 4 F G 7 % E**

questions.prompt: How many such even numbers are there in the above arrangement, each of which is immediately preceded by a letter and immediately followed by a symbol?

steps: Check each even number: it needs a letter just before it and a symbol just after it.
Such even numbers: 2 → **Two**.
solution.shortcut: Scan only the even numbers and glance at the element on each side — no need to read every element.
solution.trap: In \$ **4** F the symbol and the letter are on the wrong sides — 4 is preceded by a symbol, not a letter, so it does not count.

questions.prompt: If all the vowels are removed from the above arrangement, how many such symbols will be there in the new arrangement, each of which is immediately preceded by a number and immediately followed by a consonant?

steps:
Remove all the vowels. New arrangement (21 elements):
5 D © 8 N 3 ↑ P 2 = Q 6 # L 9 \$ 4 F G 7 %
Check each symbol: it needs a number just before it and a consonant just after it.
Such symbols: 3 → **Three**.
solution.shortcut: Scan only the symbols of the new arrangement and glance at the element on each side — no need to read every element.
solution.trap: Counting on the original arrangement gives 2 — the change creates new neighbours, so count only on the new arrangement.

questions.prompt: If the first 12 elements (from the left end) of the above arrangement are written in reverse order, which of the following will be the 5th element to the right of the 4th element from the left end?

steps:
Reverse the first 12 elements. New arrangement:
Q = 2 P ↑ 3 N I 8 © D 5 6 # O L 9 \$ 4 F G 7 % E
4th from the left end = **P**.
5th to the right of it = 4 + 5 = 9th from the left end.
9th from the left end = **8**.
solution.shortcut: Convert to one count from the left: 4th + 5 = 9th.
solution.trap: Counting the same way on the original arrangement gives **P** — rewrite the arrangement first.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the 7th element to the left of the 6th element from the right end in the above arrangement?

steps: 6th from the right end = 24 − 6 + 1 = 19th from the left end (**4**).
7th to the left of it = 19 − 7 = 12th from the left end.
12th from the left end = **Q**.
solution.shortcut: Convert to one count from the left: 19th − 7 = 12th.
solution.trap: The 6th from the right is the 19th from the left (24 − 6 + 1); using 24 − 6 = 18 lands on **=** instead.

questions.prompt: Four of the following five are alike in a certain way based on their positions in the above arrangement and so form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group?

steps: Pattern (from ©I8): take an element, then the element 2nd to the right of it, then the element 1st to the right of it.
©I8 — first element at position 3, follows it ✓
NP3 — does not follow this pattern ✗
2Q= — first element at position 10, follows it ✓
#LO — first element at position 14, follows it ✓
4GF — first element at position 19, follows it ✓
Odd one: **NP3**.
solution.shortcut: Find the first element of one option in the arrangement, read off the offsets of the other two, and test the rest with the same offsets.
solution.trap: NP3 looks right at a glance — one of its elements is one place away from where the pattern needs it.

sets.title: Alphanumeric series
sets.stimulus:
Study the following arrangement carefully and answer the questions given below.

**7 # 3 8 © 5 2 @ 9 % 6 1 & 4 ★ 7 2 £ 8 = 5 3 ↑**

questions.prompt: How many such even numbers are there in the above arrangement, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and immediately followed by a symbol?

steps: Check each even number: it needs an odd number just before it and a symbol just after it.
Such even numbers: 3 → **Three**.
solution.shortcut: Scan only the even numbers and glance at the element on each side — no need to read every element.
solution.trap: & **4** ★ does not count — it is preceded by &, not an odd number.

questions.prompt: What is the sum of all the odd numbers in the above arrangement, each of which is immediately preceded by a symbol and immediately followed by an even number?

steps: Check each odd number: it needs a symbol just before it and an even number just after it.
solution.shortcut: Mark the qualifying odd numbers while scanning once, then add only those.
solution.trap: @ **9** % does not count — it is followed by %, not an even number.

questions.prompt: If all the even numbers are removed from the above arrangement, which of the following will be the 4th element to the left of the 6th element from the right end?

steps:
Remove all the even numbers. New arrangement (17 elements):
7 # 3 © 5 @ 9 % 1 & ★ 7 £ = 5 3 ↑
6th from the right end = 17 − 6 + 1 = 12th from the left end (**7**).
4th to the left of it = 12 − 4 = 8th from the left end.
8th from the left end = **%**.
solution.shortcut: Convert to one count from the left: 12th − 4 = 8th.
solution.trap: Counting the same way on the original arrangement gives **4** — rewrite the arrangement first.

questions.prompt: How many odd numbers are there between **#** and **★** in the above arrangement?

steps: **#** is 2nd and **★** is 15th from the left end.
Elements between them: 3 8 © 5 2 @ 9 % 6 1 & 4
Odd numbers among them: 3, 5, 9, 1 → **More than three**.
solution.shortcut: Underline the two symbols, then scan only the stretch between them.
solution.trap: Do not count # or ★ themselves, and do not stop at an earlier look-alike symbol.

questions.prompt: Four of the following five are alike in a certain way based on their positions in the above arrangement and so form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group?

steps: Pattern (from #3©): take an element, then the element 1st to the right of it, then the element 3rd to the right of it.
#3© — first element at position 2, follows it ✓
52% — does not follow this pattern ✗
%6& — first element at position 10, follows it ✓
4★2 — first element at position 14, follows it ✓
£85 — first element at position 18, follows it ✓
Odd one: **52%**.
solution.shortcut: Find the first element of one option in the arrangement, read off the offsets of the other two, and test the rest with the same offsets.
solution.trap: 52% looks right at a glance — one of its elements is one place away from where the pattern needs it.

sets.title: Alphanumeric series
sets.stimulus:
Study the following arrangement carefully and answer the questions given below.

**3 8 5 2 7 4 9 1 6 3 2 8 5 7 4 6 9 2 1 5 8 3 7 4**

questions.prompt: How many such even numbers are there in the above arrangement, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and immediately followed by a perfect square?

steps: Perfect squares among the digits: 1, 4 and 9 (1 = 1 × 1).
Check each even number: it needs an odd number just before it and a perfect square just after it.
Such even numbers: 2 → **Two**.
solution.shortcut: Scan only the even numbers and glance at the element on each side — no need to read every element.
solution.trap: 3 **8** 5 does not count — it is followed by 5, not a perfect square.

questions.prompt: How many such odd numbers are there in the above arrangement, each of which is immediately preceded by an even number and immediately followed by an even number?

steps: Check each odd number: it needs an even number just before it and an even number just after it.
Such odd numbers: 4 → **More than three**.
solution.shortcut: Scan only the odd numbers and glance at the element on each side — no need to read every element.
solution.trap: 4 **9** 1 does not count — it is followed by 1, not an even number.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the 7th element to the left of the 4th element from the right end in the above arrangement?

steps: 4th from the right end = 24 − 4 + 1 = 21st from the left end (**8**).
7th to the left of it = 21 − 7 = 14th from the left end.
14th from the left end = **7**.
solution.shortcut: Convert to one count from the left: 21st − 7 = 14th.
solution.trap: The 4th from the right is the 21st from the left (24 − 4 + 1); using 24 − 4 = 20 lands on **5** instead.

questions.prompt: If all the perfect squares are removed from the above arrangement, which of the following will be the 6th element to the right of the 5th element from the left end?

steps: Perfect squares among the digits: 1, 4 and 9 (1 = 1 × 1).

Remove all the perfect squares. New arrangement (17 elements):
3 8 5 2 7 6 3 2 8 5 7 6 2 5 8 3 7
5th from the left end = **7**.
6th to the right of it = 5 + 6 = 11th from the left end.
11th from the left end = **7**.
solution.shortcut: Convert to one count from the left: 5th + 6 = 11th.
solution.trap: Counting the same way on the original arrangement gives **2** — rewrite the arrangement first.

questions.prompt: What is the sum of all the even numbers in the above arrangement, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and immediately followed by an odd number?

steps: Check each even number: it needs an odd number just before it and an odd number just after it.
solution.shortcut: Mark the qualifying even numbers while scanning once, then add only those.
solution.trap: 3 **2** 8 does not count — it is followed by 8, not an odd number.

sets.title: Alphanumeric series
sets.stimulus:
Study the following arrangement carefully and answer the questions given below.

**H 2 € A 6 S 9 \* T 4 V I 1 = L 8 C © O 5 Z ↑ 3 Y #**

questions.prompt: How many such vowels are there in the above arrangement, each of which is immediately preceded by a symbol and immediately followed by a number?

steps: Check each vowel: it needs a symbol just before it and a number just after it.
Such vowels: 2 → **Two**.
solution.shortcut: Scan only the vowels and glance at the element on each side — no need to read every element.
solution.trap: V **I** 1 does not count — it is preceded by V, not a symbol.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the 2nd number to the right of the 3rd symbol from the left end in the above arrangement?

steps: Symbols from the left end: €, \*, = → the 3rd is **=** (position 14 from the left).
Numbers to its right, in order: 8, 5, 3 …
The 2nd of them = **5**.
solution.shortcut: Mark the symbols first, then hop over everything that is not a number.
solution.trap: The 2nd element (of any kind) to the right of = is **8** — count only numbers.

questions.prompt: If all the symbols are removed from the above arrangement, which of the following will be the 5th element to the left of the 8th element from the right end?

steps:
Remove all the symbols. New arrangement (19 elements):
H 2 A 6 S 9 T 4 V I 1 L 8 C O 5 Z 3 Y
8th from the right end = 19 − 8 + 1 = 12th from the left end (**L**).
5th to the left of it = 12 − 5 = 7th from the left end.
7th from the left end = **T**.
solution.shortcut: Convert to one count from the left: 12th − 5 = 7th.
solution.trap: Counting the same way on the original arrangement gives **1** — rewrite the arrangement first.

questions.prompt: Four of the following five are alike in a certain way based on their positions in the above arrangement and so form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group?

steps: Pattern (from €62): take an element, then the element 2nd to the right of it, then the element 1st to the left of it.
€62 — first element at position 3, follows it ✓
9TS — first element at position 7, follows it ✓
I=V — first element at position 12, follows it ✓
8©= — does not follow this pattern ✗
Z35 — first element at position 21, follows it ✓
Odd one: **8©=**.
solution.shortcut: Find the first element of one option in the arrangement, read off the offsets of the other two, and test the rest with the same offsets.
solution.trap: 8©= looks right at a glance — one of its elements is one place away from where the pattern needs it.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the 3rd element to the left of the 7th element to the right of **S** in the above arrangement?

steps: **S** is 6th from the left end.
7th to the right → 13th from the left end (**1**).
3rd to the left → 10th from the left end (**4**).
solution.shortcut: Net movement = +7 −3 = +4 → 4 to the right of S.
solution.trap: Moving the other way (4 to the left) gives **2**.

sets.title: Alphanumeric series
sets.stimulus:
Study the following arrangement carefully and answer the questions given below.

**B 7 % I 4 N ↑ 9 Q 3 £ E 6 R W 1 @ 8 J U 2 & 5 X © K**

questions.prompt: How many such even numbers are there in the above arrangement, each of which is immediately followed by a symbol but not immediately preceded by an odd number?

steps: Check each even number: it needs no odd number just before it and a symbol just after it.
Such even numbers: 1 → **One**.
solution.shortcut: Scan only the even numbers and glance at the element on each side — no need to read every element.
solution.trap: I **4** N does not count — it is followed by N, not a symbol.

questions.prompt: If all the odd numbers which are immediately preceded by a consonant are removed from the above arrangement, which of the following will be the 6th element to the right of the 9th element from the left end?

steps:
Remove all the odd numbers which are immediately preceded by a consonant (judged on the arrangement before removal). New arrangement (23 elements):
B % I 4 N ↑ 9 Q £ E 6 R W @ 8 J U 2 & 5 X © K
9th from the left end = **£**.
6th to the right of it = 9 + 6 = 15th from the left end.
15th from the left end = **8**.
solution.shortcut: Convert to one count from the left: 9th + 6 = 15th.
solution.trap: Counting the same way on the original arrangement gives **W** — rewrite the arrangement first.

questions.prompt: What is the sum of all the numbers in the above arrangement, each of which is immediately preceded by a symbol and immediately followed by a letter?

steps: Check each number: it needs a symbol just before it and a letter just after it.
solution.shortcut: Mark the qualifying numbers while scanning once, then add only those.
solution.trap: I **4** N does not count — it is preceded by I, not a symbol.

questions.prompt: If the last 14 elements (at the right end) of the above arrangement are written in reverse order, which of the following will be the 8th element to the left of the 5th element from the right end?

steps:
Reverse the last 14 elements. New arrangement:
B 7 % I 4 N ↑ 9 Q 3 £ E K © X 5 & 2 U J 8 @ 1 W R 6
5th from the right end = 26 − 5 + 1 = 22nd from the left end (**@**).
8th to the left of it = 22 − 8 = 14th from the left end.
14th from the left end = **©**.
solution.shortcut: Convert to one count from the left: 22nd − 8 = 14th.
solution.trap: Counting the same way on the original arrangement gives **R** — rewrite the arrangement first.

questions.prompt: Four of the following five are alike in a certain way based on their positions in the above arrangement and so form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group?

steps: Pattern (from %IB): take an element, then the element 1st to the right of it, then the element 2nd to the left of it.
%IB — first element at position 3, follows it ✓
↑94 — first element at position 7, follows it ✓
W1R — does not follow this pattern ✗
JU@ — first element at position 19, follows it ✓
5X2 — first element at position 23, follows it ✓
Odd one: **W1R**.
solution.shortcut: Find the first element of one option in the arrangement, read off the offsets of the other two, and test the rest with the same offsets.
solution.trap: W1R looks right at a glance — one of its elements is one place away from where the pattern needs it.
